subject: Model compatibility safety net & comms cadence for v2 rollout
messages:
From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Model compatibility safety net & comms cadence for v2 rollout

Team —

Quick sync request as we finalize the v2 rollout runway: before we publish the customer notice I want to lock down the safety-net plan (what we fall back to if a customer sees a quality regression or latency spike) and the external comms cadence. Key asks:

1) Safety net mechanism: do we prefer a compatibility shim (translate v2 responses to v1 shape) or a short-term dual-serving strategy (serve v1 for pinned customers and v2 for the rest)? pros/cons from infra/latency/cost perspective.
2) Escalation ladder: who owns first-line customer triage? I propose CS (Marissa) + SRE (Ben) for triage, product (me) for triage decisions, and Eng (Grace) for mitigation. Confirm?
3) Comms cadence: draft notice + 1-week reminder + 24h cutover note. Do we want a canary pool and a pre-cutover opt-in for strategic customers (ACME)?
4) Exception handling: short list of steps to approve a temporary pin for enterprise customers; timeboxed (<=14 days) and logged.

I attached a short runbook + comm draft. Please reply with: preferred safety-net approach, owner confirmations, and any missing blockers by 11:00 PT today. If there are proposals that require leadership sign-off, flag them explicitly.

Thanks —
Ethan
Ethan Park
Director, Product 
Redwood Inference

Attachments: v2-safety-net-runbook.pdf, comm-cadence-brief.md
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model compatibility safety net & comms cadence for v2 rollout

Ethan —

Thanks for the clear asks. Quick responses: 

- Safety net: CS preference is a compatibility shim for the first 7 days for high-risk customers (preserves UX and avoids full-dual serving costs). That buys time to evaluate quality regressions. If infra says shim is too brittle, then dual-serving for a small pinned cohort.
- Escalation ladder: agree with your proposal. I will own first-line communication and SLA breach comms to the customer PM/TPM. Ben, Ben/Grace will you confirm incident runbook owners?
- Comms cadence: yes to draft notice + 1-week reminder + 24h. For ACME, let's invite them to a pre-cutover canary (opt-in) — they already asked for a heads-up. I can own the outreach.
- Exceptions: I support a 14-day timebox and a single product/CS sign-off to start; any longer requires VP sign-off.

I'll update the comm-cadence-brief with language for the ACME opt-in and share a short template for customer outreach by 12:30 PT.

Marissa
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model compatibility safety net & comms cadence for v2 rollout

Ethan / Marissa —

Operational take: compatibility shim is feasible but has caveats. Pros: minimal infra footprint, fast to deploy (we already have a small translation layer from prior experiments). Cons: introduces ongoing maintenance risk for the first 72h as we stabilize tokenization edge-cases and response field mapping. Dual-serving is more robust for quality comparisons but doubles GPUs and risks higher latency for pinned traffic unless we isolate pools.

Suggested hybrid: implement a lightweight shim as the default safety net + a dual-serving opt-in pool for strategic customers (ACME, two others). That puts most traffic through the cheap path while giving us a controlled comparison signal.

Runbook notes (attached):
- Pre-rollout: create canary pool (2r3g), enable detailed tracing for canary customers, snapshot model metrics.
- T+0..T+24h: enhanced logging + quality checks; if P95 latency > 250ms or regression delta > 3% on our eval set, trigger auto-rollback to pinned v1 for affected accounts.
- Escalation: Ben on-call -> Grace eng lead -> Ethan product decision -> Marissa customer comms.

I'll drop the rollback-checklist.xlsx in the folder and tag INF-9201. If everyone agrees, I can schedule the canary pool creation for Friday morning and we can invite ACME to opt-in.

Ben
Sr SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: rollback-checklist.xlsx

All —

I support Ben's hybrid approach. Operational notes from Eng:

- Shim implementation: we'll scope it to response-shape translation only (no model-level reranking) to reduce complexity. Expect ~2 engineer-days to build + 1 day of integration testing.
- Observability: need a short list of golden prompts (I'll work with Marissa on those) and an automated drift check that runs hourly during T+0..T+72h.
- Rollback: Engineering will own the rollback execution once product triggers it; Ben please confirm we have playbooks and permissions set so rollback can proceed without blocked approvals during an incident window.

Action items:
- Marissa: customer outreach templates for ACME opt-in (deliver by 12:30 PT) — ACK
- Ben: schedule canary pool creation (FRI morning) and drop runbook into the shared folder — ACK
- Ethan: finalize external notice and send to Legal for a quick review (I recommend a 48h review window) — can you send by EOD?

I'll start the shim spike tomorrow and post progress in INF-9201.

Grace
